scope.flow: Campaign duration validation during createCampaign/overrideCampaign (epoch alignment)
scope.environment: Merkl DistributionCreator Solidity contract on EVM with an off-chain epoch-based indexing engine

statements.text: The CampaignParameters documentation explicitly states a strict requirement that the campaign duration be a multiple of EPOCH_DURATION.
The Merkl protocol relies on discrete 1-hour epochs (EPOCH_DURATION) for reward calculation and distribution.
DistributionCreator exposes campaign creation through _createCampaign and overrideCampaign.
A campaign creator controls the duration value supplied when creating a campaign.
A creator calls createCampaign with a duration of 5400 seconds (1.5 hours), which is not a multiple of EPOCH_DURATION.
The duration validation in _createCampaign and overrideCampaign enforces only the minimum duration and omits the multiple-of-EPOCH_DURATION check, so no bound rejects the misaligned duration.
The campaign is accepted and created with a duration covering one full epoch and one half-epoch.
The off-chain indexing engine may reject the campaign (locking user funds) or drop the final partial epoch (losing user rewards).
Inferred: campaign creation should reject any duration that is not a multiple of EPOCH_DURATION before the campaign is created, keeping campaigns aligned to the protocol's epoch schedule.
EPOCH_DURATION is one hour and the off-chain indexing engine expects epoch-aligned campaign durations.

ambiguities: Whether campaign creation is permissionless or restricted to authorized creators is not stated.
Exact numeric value of EPOCH_DURATION is not given (report only states 1-hour epochs).
No evidence the off-chain indexing engine actually rejects or miscomputes misaligned durations.
Access control and caller restrictions on overrideCampaign are unspecified.
No confirmed incident or realized loss; downstream effects are stated as possible.
